title: Bitcoin miners pay Paraguay $350 million a year, but AI is pushing them out
summary: Title: Bitcoin and AI are fighting a $350 million battle over a dam in Paraguay URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/11/13/bitcoin-miners-pay-paraguay-usd350-million-a-year-but-ai-is-pushing-them-out Published Time: 2026-11-13T23:30:00.000Z Markdown Content: Updated Nov 14, 2026, 12:36 a.m. EST Published Nov 13, 2026, 6:30 p.m. EST 5 min read Summary * Paraguay’s state utility plans to let all special cryptocurrency power contracts expire on Dec. 31, 2027, as domestic electricity demand grows and artificial intelligence companies compete for cheap hydropower. * Utility engineers have proposed capping combined electricity allocations for mining, A.I. and data centers at 700 megawatts and auctioning power at higher rates, threatening miners that currently hold about 944 megawatts. * A company linked to the planned $12 billion Iguazú AI City has secured a 15-year power contract, while HIVE Digital Technologies faces uncertainty over Paraguayan sites that house roughly 77 percent of its operating mining capacity. For years, the rhythmic hum of industrial cooling fans has echoed across a subtropical stretch of eastern Paraguay, where rows of specialized computers churn out bitcoin [BTC$67,152.11](https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin) using some of the cheapest electricity on earth. Drawn by surplus hydropower from the 14,000-megawatt Itaipu Dam on the Brazilian border, foreign crypto companies struck lucrative deals with Paraguay’s state utility, turning excess energy into roughly $350 million in annual public revenue and making the country the world’s fourth-largest Bitcoin mining hub. But that bargain is now unraveling. Paraguay’s national power company, ANDE, plans to let every special crypto contract expire on Dec. 31, 2027, a deadline officials have declared nonnegotiable, as domestic electricity demand surges and a new, even hungrier competitor arrives: Artificial intelligence.
